label: because: giving a reason
note: CLOSED by chapter 73, together with ML-A1-Q-07. Both notes were accurate and both were verified: enthukondu, kaaranam and enthukondennaal each returned ZERO files across the whole corpus. THE TWO POINTS ARE ONE PIECE OF WORK and the notes said so -- cause could be handled in NEITHER direction, so closing one without the other would have left a learner able to ask a question nobody could answer or to answer one nobody could ask. MOST OF THE CHAPTER IS BUILT FROM MATERIAL THE READER ALREADY HAS. Malayalam has no separate word for why: entukondu is chapter two's entu (what) plus kondu, the ending meaning by means of, so the question literally asks 'by what'. The written because, entukondennaal, then carries that whole question word visibly at its front. KAARANAM IS THE ONE FOR SPEECH and is a noun first -- a reason, a cause -- taken whole from Sanskrit kaarana, which puts it beside cinta and suprabhaatam as nouns this track borrows unreshaped. THE TAIL OF ENTUKONDENNAAL IS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN APART. Its -ennaal can be read as the but-word ML-C64 teaches or as a conditional of the saying-verb, and grammars differ; the lesson says so rather than picking one. That is the same refusal this campaign applies to an unsourced stroke order.
